name: Madewell
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $93 (women's price pass, 2026-10-22)
why: Denim-led women's and men's clothing, knitwear, outerwear, shoes and bags, sold through its own stores and website.

ownership.owner: J.Crew Group, LLC (private; brand introduced 2006 inside J.Crew; investor page says J.Crew Group runs J.Crew, J.Crew Factory and Madewell)

quote.q: We're inspired by the belief that great denim is forever, foundational pieces can be emotional, and effortless style is for every day.

opview: “We're inspired by the belief that great denim is forever, foundational pieces can be emotional, and effortless style is for every day.” — Madewell (house voice, About page), About Madewell, madewell.com

facts_read.source: madewell.com about, quality, materials, lookbook pages; investors.madewell.com; vinted.com brand filter; therealreal.com; bcorporation.net and global-standard.org directories

T-shirt.lp: The Easy V-Neck Tee in Soft Slub
T-shirt.hp: Easy Crewneck Long-Sleeve Tee in Sunday Slub

Sweater.lp: The Arden Crewneck Sweater in 100% Cotton

price_read.sublines: Madewell own label only; outside brands left out (Frye, Birkenstock, Keds, Reebok, Asics, Minnetonka, LESET, Banjanan); NYPL and Kaihara collaborations never a high

doors.note: 164 listed = 162 open or opening + 2 'Temporarily Closed' (Scottsdale 7014 E Camelback; Southdale Edina) held out for Sebastian's ruling. us_outlets=0 means none of the 164 is labelled outlet; the locator has no format field. Concessions and stockists not on this locator so NC. 2 of the 162 are Coming Soon (San Tan Village Gilbert AZ; Cobble Hill NY). 7 are men's-only Madewell shops

fibre.sample: 79 of 231 style codes, stratified across the ten category pages in proportion to size (even spacing within each category). Totals are what the category pages yi

tech_evidence.names: TENCEL(TM) Lyocell and LENZING(TM) ECOVERO(TM) viscose (Lenzing, licensed); own-named cloths Airy Denim, Super Stretch Denim, Comfort Stretch, SoftWool (100% merino), Apres Fleece; third-party Cone and Orta denim named on some jeans pages
tech_evidence.owned: licensed (TENCEL, ECOVERO from Lenzing; Regenagri is a farm certification, not a cloth); the other names are Madewell's own marketing names for ordinary cotton, wool and polyester cloths
tech_evidence.share: lyocell in 11 of 79 sampled (13.9%); a named stretch denim (Super Stretch or Comfort Stretch) on 9 of 25 sampled jeans; none is a performance fabric

craft_evidence.owned: NONE (no own factory found; Madewell's parent filed in its last 10-K on the investors site, fiscal 2017, that it owns no manufacturing facilities; that filing is old and I found no newer one)
craft_evidence.makers: NONE (product pages say only "Imported" and never name a factory)
craft_evidence.mills: partial (Cone denim on 1 and Orta denim on 1 of 25 sampled jeans pages; ISKO named in trade press as a bluesign denim partner, not on the pages I read; the quality page says only "the best denim mills
craft_evidence.madein: 0% (79 of 79 sampled pages say "Imported."; the quality page says over 90% of denim is made in Fair Trade Certified fact
craft_evidence.heritage: dated, not placed: "Introduced in 2006, Madewell is a premium denim brand" (about page); no founding place, workshop or maker named
craft_evidence.process: no (the quality hub covers sourcing standards: Regenagri cotton, Good Cashmere Standard, Leather Working Group, Fair Trade; it does not describe how anything is made)
craft_evidence.reasoning: Madewell states sourcing standards and a share of Fair Trade Certified denim factories but names no factory, owns none, and every sampled product page says only "Imported". Mills are named on 2 of 25 sampled jeans pages (Cone, Orta). That is a stated standard with little checkable beyond it, so a 2; it would move to 3 if the mills or factories were named across the denim range.
